clusters.title: [Impact] KB5099414 on Config1 - Shell servicing touches WinExe launch identity
clusters.body:
<!-- impact:shell-launch:Config1 -->

Impact analysis conducted on source code version:

- https://github.com/defrances/HostApplication - commit `22b249a754b849dac151e976b533f60994fc6098`

## Updates applicable for this product configuration

| Title | Package | CVEs | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows Shell Spoofing Vulnerability | [KB5099414](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-32202) | CVE-2026-32202 | Low Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Config1`
- Model / role: `CTConsole-A300` / `ct-imaging-workstation`
- Deployment group: `imaging-ct`
- OS: `Windows 11 IoT Enterprise` build `10.0.22621.2500`
- Clinical criticality: `high`
- Network exposure: `restricted_lan`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `C` | `C` | `C` |
| Product | `L` | `L` | `L` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

`HostApplication.csproj` `OutputType=WinExe` and `app.manifest` `assemblyIdentity` name `HostApplication` for shell launch (Windows 10 compatibility GUID in manifest).

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** Not required. Shell components are OS-provided; product does not embed shell32.
- **If we install: App may break.** App may break. Shell updates can change Explorer launch/spoofing behavior for the WinExe identity.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Station stays exposed. Shell spoofing issues remain; in-app logic still runs if the exe is started.
- **Compatibility: Compatible.** Compatible. Builds already launch on current lab shell with manifest identity on `main`.

### Conclusions

Respect FindUpdates Low Prio/HOLD on blocked configs; elsewhere validate manual launch smoke only.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

Shell spoofing CVEs patch Windows Shell. No Shell imports in Core; coupling is WinExe launch trust only.

## Product Risk assessment

- Functions touched: Operator launch of the WinExe; notes/bulletin features unchanged.
- Potential hazards: None identified for product logic on `main`; host privilege flaws remain a workstation concern.
- Install vs skip: Installing patches host components cited above; skipping leaves host exposure while the self-contained Host Application exe and `NoteStore`/`MainViewModel` contracts remain runnable.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- `None. No documented test covers Shell launch or spoofing.`

### Gap Analysis

- No Shell launch automation in `docs/test-plan.md`.

## Recommendation

Low Prio for lab tracking on `Config1`. This analysis does not authorize production deployment.

| Desktop Window Manager Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5099535](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-50692) | CVE-2026-50692 | Install - High Prio |

- Product configuration: `Config2`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `H` | `M` | `H` |
| Product | `L` | `L` | `L` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

Desktop Window Manager composition affects WPF rendering for `MainWindow.xaml`; `app.manifest` declares PerMonitorV2 DPI awareness.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** Not required. DWM is host-side; self-contained publish embeds .NET runtime separately from DWM patches.
- **If we install: App may break.** App may break. DWM/Core library updates can alter WPF composition/DPI visibility after install.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Station stays exposed. DWM flaws remain while the exe still launches.
- **Compatibility: Compatible.** Compatible. WPF client already runs against current lab DWM versions.

### Conclusions

Host DWM patch does not change bundled runtime; optional UI smoke after reboot.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

DWM-related CVEs patch Desktop Window Manager on Windows. No DWM dependency in `HostApplication.Core`; WPF uses the compositor indirectly.

## Product Risk assessment

- Functions touched: WPF chrome in `MainWindow.xaml`. Core notes/TLS logic unchanged.
- Potential hazards: None identified for product logic on `main`; host privilege flaws remain a workstation concern.
- Install vs skip: Installing patches host components cited above; skipping leaves host exposure while the self-contained Host Application exe and `NoteStore`/`MainViewModel` contracts remain runnable.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- `None. No documented test covers DWM composition changes.`

### Gap Analysis

- No visual regression automation for WPF after graphics stack updates.

## Recommendation

Install - High Prio for lab tracking on `Config2`. This analysis does not authorize production deployment.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

`NoteStore.cs` uses `File.ReadAllText` / `File.WriteAllText` on `%AppData%\HostApplication\notes.txt`; `NoteStoreTests.cs` locks the contract.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** Not required. Notes use BCL file APIs; NTFS.sys is not loaded as a product dependency.
- **If we install: Compatible with the app.** Compatible with the app. NTFS KB patches the host volume driver, not the self-contained exe or `NoteStore` API.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Station stays exposed. NTFS flaws remain on the AppData volume while notes I/O still works.
- **Compatibility: Compatible.** Compatible. `TC-SMOKE-NOTES` and unit tests already exercise file I/O on lab NTFS.

### Conclusions

KB reduces host filesystem risk on the volume holding AppData; product paths unchanged.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

NTFS RCE CVEs target the Windows NTFS driver. Source scan shows only `NoteStore.cs` BCL calls—no NTFS driver in the product.

## Product Risk assessment

- Functions touched: Notes load/save/export via `NoteStore` and `MainViewModel` commands.
- Potential hazards: None identified for product logic on `main`; host privilege flaws remain a workstation concern.
- Install vs skip: Installing patches host components cited above; skipping leaves host exposure while the self-contained Host Application exe and `NoteStore`/`MainViewModel` contracts remain runnable.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- `TC-UNIT-NOTES-EMPTY`
- `TC-UNIT-NOTES-PATH`
- `TC-SMOKE-NOTES`

### Gap Analysis

- None identified.

## Recommendation

Install - High Prio for lab tracking on `Config2`. This analysis does not authorize production deployment.

| Windows Win32k Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5099536](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-54112) | CVE-2026-54112 | Install - High Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Config2`
- Model / role: `LabBench-L110` / `lab-analysis-workstation`
- Deployment group: `lab-ring-0`
- OS: `Windows 11 IoT Enterprise` build `10.0.26100.4200`
- Clinical criticality: `high`
- Network exposure: `restricted_lan`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `H` | `H` | `H` |
| Product | `L` | `L` | `L` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

WPF windowing on `MainWindow.xaml` (`UseWPF` in `HostApplication.csproj`) and `app.manifest` (`dpiAware` true/pm, `dpiAwareness` PerMonitorV2) depend on the host Win32k/windowing stack.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** Not required. CI publishes `--self-contained true` for `win-x64` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`); Win32k is not a product `PackageReference`.
- **If we install: App may break.** App may break. Host Win32k updates can change DPI/windowing behavior for WPF after reboot (`MainWindow.xaml`, `app.manifest` PerMonitorV2).
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Station stays exposed. Win32k privilege issues remain on the host while the WPF client still starts.
- **Compatibility: Compatible.** Compatible. Current `main` runs on today's lab builds; KB bits are outside the bundled exe.

### Conclusions

Install for host hardening if policy allows; validate WPF startup and DPI smoke after reboot.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

Win32k elevation-of-privilege CVEs patch the Windows windowing kernel stack. SBOM and source scan show no Win32k module in product code—coupling is via WPF host rendering only.

## Product Risk assessment

- Functions touched: WPF UI layout/DPI (`MainWindow.xaml`, `app.manifest`). Notes and bulletin HTTPS paths are indirect.
- Potential hazards: None identified for product logic on `main`; host privilege flaws remain a workstation concern.
- Install vs skip: Installing patches host components cited above; skipping leaves host exposure while the self-contained Host Application exe and `NoteStore`/`MainViewModel` contracts remain runnable.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- `None. No documented test covers Win32k/DPI host changes.`

### Gap Analysis

- No UI automation or per-monitor DPI regression in `docs/test-plan.md`.

## Recommendation

Install - High Prio for lab tracking on `Config2`. This analysis does not authorize production deployment.

findings.title: Vendor bulletin HTTPS accepts any server certificate
findings.evidence: src/HostApplication.Core/InsecureVendorBulletinClient.cs: AcceptAnyServerCertificate returns sslPolicyErrors == SslPolicyErrors.None; Marker is TLS_CERTIFICATE_VALIDATED (no INTENTIONAL_SKILL_TEST_VULNERABILITY). TC-REG-TLS-CALLBACK asserts rejection when chain is invalid. Catalog and docs/mds2.md MDS2-TLS row are stale relative to main; code on main enforces certificate validation.

findings.title: Notes stored as plaintext in user AppData
findings.evidence: src/HostApplication.Core/NoteStore.cs writes UTF-8 plaintext under %AppData%\HostApplication\notes.txt with no network export path in the save/load API. inputs/mds2.md MDS2-DATA: met — local notes only, no PHI, no remote storage.

findings.title: No inbound network listener
findings.evidence: No HttpListener, Kestrel, or TcpListener in repository; only optional outbound HTTPS via InsecureVendorBulletinClient.FetchAsync. inputs/mds2.md MDS2-NET: met — no inbound ports.
